newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE re-lists and amends Dec 1997 Bund contract.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE re-lists and amends Dec 1997 Bund contract.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Thursday it had re-listed the German government bond December 1997 futures contract.
At the same time, LIFFE said it had decided to increase the range of deliverable maturity criteria of 8-1/2 to 10-1/2 remaining years to maturity.
The Bund contract was previously suspended on March 24, 1997 following a Bundesbank announcement indicating a change in issuance pattern in the 10-year sector of the yield curve.
"LIFFE suspended the Bund contract when the Bundesbank indicated a change in the underlying cash market," Daniel Hodson, chief executive at LIFFE said in a statement.

"The clean and proper suspension of the Bund contract enabled LIFFE to consult the market regarding the deliverable criteria and re-list it with a maturity of 8-1/2 to 10-1/2 years, thereby providing the most suitable contract for our members and their clients," he said.
The Bundesbank will auction a new 10-year benchmark Bund in April 1997 with slightly in excess of 10 years to maturity at issue, LIFFE said.
